title: Ohio Immigrant Alliance: 22 ICE/CBP Agent Sexual Violence Cases in First 8 Months of 2026
excerpt: An investigation by the Ohio Immigrant Alliance, reported by PunchUp and The Daily Beast, documented 22 cases of ICE and CBP agents charged or convicted for sexual violence in the first eight months of 2026 — doubling the previous annual high and representing nearly a quarter of a 44-year dataset. The report linked the surge to rapid hiring and weakened vetting.
content:
The Ohio Immigrant Alliance published an investigation in August 2026, reported by PunchUp and The Daily Beast, documenting a dramatic surge in ICE and Customs and Border Protection agents charged, convicted, or sentenced for sexual violence.

The alliance documented 14 cases from all of 2025, and another 22 cases during just the first eight months of 2026. Together, these cases represent nearly a quarter of the alliance's entire 44-year dataset. The previous annual high was 11 cases in 2024.

  • The report found that DHS hired, retained, and in some cases promoted immigration agents despite warning signs of violent or predatory behavior.
  • The alliance said the increase could reflect greater scrutiny, rapid hiring, weaker vetting, a larger workforce, more offending — or a combination of factors.
  • Investigators documented agents using their authority and access to sexually assault, abuse, or stalk women and children.

The alliance called on Congress to freeze ICE and Border Patrol hiring and rescreen the entire workforce for histories of domestic violence, sexual violence, and extremist activity. It also demanded mandatory reporting of criminal charges, automatic dismissal following conviction, and independent watchdogs with subpoena authority.
source: The Daily Beast / PunchUp / Ohio Immigrant Alliance
